apps.name: Photos Backup
apps.localizedDescription:
## What's new

### Live Photo motion is now on by default
**Back Up Live Photo Motion** now starts on. The Google Photos app's Free up space only offers a Live Photo once its motion is attached. If you turned the setting off, it stays off.

After updating, the motion of every Live Photo you already backed up is uploaded once in the background, a few MB each.

### New settings, all off by default
- **Back Up Portrait Originals.** An edited Portrait photo is uploaded as its edit, with the blur rendered in. With this on, the camera's original is also uploaded, and it keeps the depth data, so after downloading it you can change the focus and depth in Photos again. It also covers photos the camera captured depth for so Portrait can be turned on later. Each edited photo is checked once, and only those with depth are uploaded.
- **Back Up Video Originals.** Uploads the camera's original of every edited video, including each Cinematic video, which the camera always saves as edited. The Google Photos app may show a Cinematic video as not backed up until its original is in the account, so its Free up space can't remove it. Each edited video then appears twice in Google Photos, and some Cinematic originals don't play in the Google Photos iPhone app. Based on [g8row/PhotosBackup#38](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/pull/38) by Sailesh Dahal.
- **Allow Re-upload** (Settings → Re-check). Shows **Re-upload Selected Albums** and **Re-upload a Folder…**. These upload items again even where Google Photos already has them, using your current Storage Saver and storage quota settings. They're meant for photos that use your Google storage because they were uploaded another way. Based on [g8row/PhotosBackup#30](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/pull/30) by Josip Papež; folder support is new here.

## Before you turn these on
- **Re-upload is unproven.** Google Photos may keep the copy it already has, and a re-upload takes as long and uses as much data as the first backup. Try one small album or folder first, and compare your Google storage before and after.
- **Turning on an originals setting has a one-time cost.** It also covers items you backed up earlier, so the first run can be large: gigabytes for Video Originals on a library with many Cinematic videos.
- **Not yet tried on a device:**
  - getting the focus and depth back from a downloaded Portrait original
  - Re-upload and Re-upload a Folder against a live account

  The video originals change was tested on a device by its author. In this release, every build compiles, but the unit tests have not been run on these changes.

## Install
Unsigned IPA: sideload it with SideStore or AltStore. Check the download against `PhotosBackup.ipa.sha256`.
